keyframe_review.note: 11.9 k km2 (bbox 4.0-5.8 E, 50.4-51.8 N): Brabant between Leuven, Brussels, Antwerp and 's-Hertogenbosch ('The four capitals were Leuven, Brussels, Antwerp and 's-Hertogenbosch'). The page gives no infobox area; the gazetteer's Brabant region is 13.2 k km2. 'the city of Mechelen formed an independent state along with the Land of Heist-op-den-Berg and Gestel' (undated); the outline may include that enclave and is not corrected.

11.9 k km2 holds only until Limburg: 'The Duchy of Limburg was added to the Duchy of Brabant in 1289' (Battle of Worringen page; the Duchy of Brabant page: 'After the Battle of Worringen in 1288, the dukes of Brabant also acquired the Duchy of Limburg'). Cliopatria adds Limburg only in 1294, five years late. The outline stands for 1272-1288.

correction.text: Brabant with the Duchy of Limburg and the Overmaas lands, as Cliopatria draws them from 1294

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1289-1293: Brabant with Limburg. The 1.8 k km2 that Cliopatria adds in 1294 lie at 5.75-6.02 E, 50.5-51.0 N, which fits the Overmaas lands named by the Duchy of Brabant page: 'the "Overmaas" lands Dalhem, Valkenburg and Herzogenrath'.
13.2 k km2 for 1294-1304: Brabant with Limburg and Overmaas ('included since 1288 also the Duchy of Limburg' in the page's note; the Worringen page dates the addition to 1289). No infobox area.

13.1 k km2 for 1305-1401, the same outline. Joanna was 'a ruling duchess of Brabant from 1355 until her death' with a Joyous Entry 'arrived at in January 1356' (the Duchy of Brabant page has 'In 1354 Duke John III of Brabant granted a Joyous Entry': the pages disagree). 'a military incursion in 1356 into Brabant by Louis II of Flanders' ended in 'the humiliating Treaty of Ath, which ceded Mechelen and Antwerp to Louis'; the page gives no year for the treaty or for the return of the cities, and Cliopatria keeps both inside the outline throughout: unverified, page budget.

14.1 k km2: the usual 13.1 k plus 1.3 k km2 in the south at 4.25-4.57 E, 49.5-49.8 N (the French Ardennes on the map), which no page opened mentions: unverified, page budget. Anthony, Joanna's great-nephew, inherited 'the Duchy of Brabant, Lothier, and Limburg' when she 'died childless in 1406'; he married Elisabeth of Görlitz, 'duchess of Luxembourg', on 16 July 1409 and is listed as 'Co- Duke of Luxemburg (1411-1415)', a personal union that the outline does not show and that this dossier does not draw. The strip is carried by confidence-1 ledger events.

correction.text: Brabant with Limburg, 13.1 k km2, without Luxembourg and without the 1402 strip

keyframe_review.note: 23.3 k km2 for 1415-1421 is Brabant (13.1 k) plus Luxembourg (10.2 k, the same cells as Cliopatria's later Duchy of Luxembourg shape). The pages say otherwise: Anthony, Duke of Brabant and co-duke of Luxembourg, was 'killed at the battle of Agincourt' on 25 October 1415 and John IV took Brabant; the Duchy of Luxembourg page gives '1415-1419: Elizabeth of Görlitz' ('In 1411, Sigismund of Luxembourg lost the duchy to his niece Elisabeth') for Luxembourg. Luxembourg is removed here and belongs to the duchy-of-luxembourg dossier; the 1402 southern strip also leaves the outline in 1415.
13.1 k km2 for 1422-1428: the 1305-1401 outline again (Brabant and Limburg). No page opened dates any change; John IV is the duke ('John IV, Duke of Brabant (1403-1427)', Anthony page).
13.2 k km2 for 1429-1430, the last outline. 'In 1430 the Duchies of Lower Lotharingia, Brabant and Limburg were inherited by' Philip the Good; infobox 'Inherited by Duchy of Burgundy: 1430'.

The region is Cliopatria's 1294 outline minus its 1272 one (Overmaas, 1.8 k km2); the Duchy of Brabant page names 'the "Overmaas" lands Dalhem, Valkenburg and Herzogenrath'.

ledger.note: 1289: the Limburg contest ends with the annexation ('The Duchy of Limburg was added to the Duchy of Brabant in 1289'); Guelders renounced its claims.

region.text: a 1.3 k km2 strip in the south that Cliopatria adds in 1402

ledger.note: 1402: a southern strip joins Brabant in Cliopatria's outline. Page silent: the Anthony, Joanna and Brabant pages name no land in the French Ardennes. The region is Cliopatria's 1402 outline minus its 1422 one (1.3 k km2 at 4.25-4.57 E, 49.5-49.8 N).

1406: Anthony of Burgundy becomes Duke of Brabant. 'When his great-aunt Joanna died childless in 1406, Anthony inherited the Duchy of Brabant, Lothier, and Limburg.' A new dynasty (a cadet of Burgundy) in the same state; Joanna had been duchess 'from 1355 until her death'.

1415: the southern strip leaves Brabant in Cliopatria's outline. Page silent; the year coincides with Anthony's death at Agincourt on 25 October 1415 ('Anthony, Duke of Brabant (21 August 1384 - 25 October 1415)'), but no page ties the strip to him.

1430: Brabant passes to Philip the Good of Burgundy. 'In 1430 the Duchies of Lower Lotharingia, Brabant and Limburg were inherited by' Philip the Good; infobox 'Inherited by Duchy of Burgundy: 1430'. The page gives no day.

wars.name: War of the Limburg Succession (Battle of Worringen)

zones.text: the Duchy of Limburg and the Overmaas lands

wars.outcome: Brabant won on 5 June 1288: 'Archbishop Siegfried was taken prisoner by John of Brabant and delivered to Adolf of Berg', 'Reginald of Guelders was released after he had renounced all claims to the Duchy of Limburg', and 'The Duchy of Limburg was added to the Duchy of Brabant in 1289'; 'The Battle of Worringen meant a rise in the power of Brabant, Berg and Mark'.
wars.note: The war of the Limburg succession (claims bought in September 1283). The page says Count Henry of Luxembourg 'and two of his brothers' died in the battle but not on which side he stood, so his side is not stated here. 'the City of Cologne gained its independence from the Archbishopric'.

wars.name: Flemish invasion of Brabant
wars.outcome: A 'military incursion in 1356 into Brabant by Louis II of Flanders' ended with 'the humiliating Treaty of Ath, which ceded Mechelen and Antwerp to Louis'; the page gives no year for the treaty and Cliopatria's outline does not show the loss.
wars.note: The name is descriptive: the war's own Wikipedia article was not opened. The end year is unknown, so no contest events are entered.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey is dated on the pages opened. The Limburg frontier follows the Worringen settlement of 1288-1289 and the enclaves (Mechelen) are not drawn; Cliopatria's outlines are approximate throughout.

notes:
BRABANT. Cliopatria row 'County of Brabant' (1260-1430) is the Duchy of Brabant; its Wikipedia field 'Landgraviate of Brabant' is the pre-1183 predecessor, so the dossier gives 'Duchy of Brabant' (the article opened). The dossier starts at 1260 where the row starts; the duchy was established in 1183 (infobox) and the earlier years are not reviewed.

CORRECTIONS. (1) Limburg and the Overmaas lands (1.8 k km2 at 5.75-6.02 E, 50.5-51.0 N) were added in 1289, not 1294 (new keyframe 1289-1293). (2) Cliopatria's 1415-1421 outline contains Luxembourg (10.2 k km2, cell for cell the later Duchy of Luxembourg shape); the pages show Anthony as co-duke of Luxembourg only 1411-1415 and Elizabeth of Görlitz as holder from 1415, so Luxembourg is removed (verdict adjust). Cliopatria then puts Luxembourg inside its Duchy of Bavaria shapes 1422-1428 and in its own row only from 1429: the duchy-of-luxembourg dossier should cover 1411-1428. (3) A 1.3 k km2 strip in the French Ardennes (4.25-4.57 E, 49.5-49.8 N) joins the outline in 1402 and leaves in 1415; no page opened mentions it, so it stays as drawn and is bridged at confidence 1.

PAGE BUDGET (up to 5): the Duchy of Brabant, Battle of Worringen, Anthony, Joanna and Duchy of Luxembourg pages were opened. The Brabant article is thin: it gives no area, no dukes' dates (John I, Joanna, Wenceslaus, Anthony, John IV, Philip of Saint-Pol), nothing on Luxembourg or Jacqueline of Bavaria's war and no 4 August 1430 day. The Joanna page gives no year for the Treaty of Ath or for the return of Mechelen and Antwerp, and the 1356 Flemish incursion is therefore listed as a war with no zone or contest events. Page conflicts: the Duchy page has the Joyous Entry in 1354 (under John III), the Joanna page in January 1356. Not entered because no page opened gives it: the union with Luxembourg under Wenceslaus (1355-1383), the Burgundian treaty of 1390, Brabant's relations with Holland and Guelders.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: duchy-of-limburg (to 1288), duchy-of-guelders (Gelre), county-of-hainaut (also for the Holland dossier). The duchy-of-burgundy dossier (eu-10) must start Brabant, Lothier and Limburg in 1430-1431; Cliopatria's Burgundy shape of 1431 (71.3 k km2) is the first to include them. Family 'france' is chosen because the colour registry keeps the Netherlands orange and Belgium yellow as exceptions inside it; the colour agent decides.
